passages.text: “I have made a covenant with my eyes. How then could I gaze with desire at a virgin?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a righteous man.
Job says, “I have made a covenant with my eyes.”
I promised myself to control what I look at.
I will not look at a young woman with desire.
I choose to keep my thoughts pure.
I choose to avoid temptation.
passages.original: בְּ֭רִית כָּרַ֣תִּי לְעֵינָ֑י וּמָ֥ה אֶ֝תְבּוֹנֵ֗ן עַל־ בְּתוּלָֽה׃

passages.text: For what is the allotment of God from above, or the heritage from the Almighty on high?
passages.sermon:
God is above all.
The Almighty is on high.
God gives an allotment from above.
The Almighty gives a heritage from on high.
What is this allotment?
What is this heritage?
passages.original: וּמֶ֤ה׀ חֵ֣לֶק אֱל֣וֹהַּ מִמָּ֑עַל וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת שַׁ֝דַּ֗י מִמְּרֹמִֽים׃

passages.text: Does not disaster come to the unjust and calamity to the workers of iniquity?
passages.sermon: God punishes the unjust.\r\nGod brings disaster to those who do evil.\r\nGod sends calamity to people who commit iniquity.
passages.original: הֲלֹא־ אֵ֥יד לְעַוָּ֑ל וְ֝נֵ֗כֶר לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

passages.text: Does He not see my ways and count my every step?
passages.sermon: God is the Almighty.\r\nGod sees my ways.\r\nGod counts every step I take.
passages.original: הֲלֹא־ ה֭וּא יִרְאֶ֣ה דְרָכָ֑י וְֽכָל־ צְעָדַ֥י יִסְפּֽוֹר׃

passages.text: If I have walked in falsehood or my foot has rushed to deceit, let God weigh me with honest scales, that He may know my integrity.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a righteous man.
Job says, "If I have walked in falsehood."
He says, "If my foot has hurried to deceit."
He asks God to weigh him with honest scales.
He wants God to know his integrity.
passages.original: אִם־ הָלַ֥כְתִּי עִם־ שָׁ֑וְא וַתַּ֖חַשׁ עַל־ מִרְמָ֣ה רַגְלִֽי׃ יִשְׁקְלֵ֥נִי בְמֹאזְנֵי־ צֶ֑דֶק וְיֵדַ֥ע אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ תֻּמָּתִֽי׃

passages.text: If my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, or if impurity has stuck to my hands, then may another eat what I have sown, and may my crops be uprooted.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks here.
Job is a righteous man.
Job says, "If my steps have turned from the right path, let it be known."
"If my heart has followed my eyes, let it be known."
"If impurity has stuck to my hands, let it be known."
"If I have done these things, let another person eat what I have planted."
"Let others uproot my crops."
passages.original: אִ֥ם תִּטֶּ֣ה אַשֻּׁרִי֮ מִנִּ֪י הַ֫דָּ֥רֶךְ וְאַחַ֣ר עֵ֭ינַי הָלַ֣ךְ לִבִּ֑י וּ֝בְכַפַּ֗י דָּ֣בַק מֻאֽוּם׃פ אֶ֭זְרְעָה וְאַחֵ֣ר יֹאכֵ֑ל וְֽצֶאֱצָאַ֥י יְשֹׁרָֽשׁוּ׃

passages.text: If my heart has been enticed by my neighbor’s wife, or I have lurked at his door, then may my own wife grind grain for another, and may other men sleep with her.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a righteous man.
Job says, “If my heart has desired my neighbor’s wife,
or if I have waited secretly at my neighbor’s door,
then let my wife grind grain for another man.
Let other men sleep with her.”
passages.original: אִם־ נִפְתָּ֣ה לִ֭בִּי עַל־ אִשָּׁ֑ה וְעַל־ פֶּ֖תַח רֵעִ֣י אָרָֽבְתִּי׃ תִּטְחַ֣ן לְאַחֵ֣ר אִשְׁתִּ֑י וְ֝עָלֶ֗יהָ יִכְרְע֥וּן אֲחֵרִֽין׃

passages.text: For that would be a heinous crime, an iniquity to be judged.
passages.sermon: This act is a heinous crime.\r\nThis act is a serious sin.\r\nGod will judge this sin.
passages.original: כִּי־ הוּא זִמָּ֑ה וְהִיא עָוֺ֥ן פְּלִילִֽים׃

passages.text: For it is a fire that burns down to Abaddon; it would root out my entire harvest.
passages.sermon:
This sin is like a fire.
The fire burns until everything is destroyed.
The fire reaches even to Abaddon, the place of destruction.
This fire would destroy all my harvest.
It would take away everything I have produced.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אֵ֣שׁ הִ֭יא עַד־ אֲבַדּ֣וֹן תֹּאכֵ֑ל וּֽבְכָל־ תְּב֖וּאָתִ֣י תְשָׁרֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: If I have rejected the cause of my manservant or maidservant when they made a complaint against me, what will I do when God rises to judge? How will I answer when called to account?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a righteous man.
Job considers how he treats his servants.
If I reject the case of my male servant when he complains against me, I do wrong.
If I reject the case of my female servant when she complains against me, I do wrong.
God will rise to judge all people.
If I act unjustly, what will I do when God judges me?
If God calls me to account, how will I answer Him?
passages.original: אִם־ אֶמְאַ֗ס מִשְׁפַּ֣ט עַ֭בְדִּי וַאֲמָתִ֑י בְּ֝רִבָ֗ם עִמָּדִֽי׃ וּמָ֣ה אֶֽ֭עֱשֶׂה כִּֽי־ יָק֣וּם אֵ֑ל וְכִֽי־ יִ֝פְקֹ֗ד מָ֣ה אֲשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Did not He who made me in the womb also make them? Did not the same One form us in the womb?
passages.sermon:
God made me in the womb.
God also made them in the womb.
The same God formed us both.
God created us together before we were born.
passages.original: הֲ‍ֽ֝לֹא־ בַ֭בֶּטֶן עֹשֵׂ֣נִי עָשָׂ֑הוּ וַ֝יְכֻנֶ֗נּוּ בָּרֶ֥חֶם אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: If I have denied the desires of the poor or allowed the widow’s eyes to fail, if I have eaten my morsel alone, not sharing it with the fatherless— though from my youth I reared him as would a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow— if I have seen one perish for lack of clothing, or a needy man without a cloak, if his heart has not blessed me for warming him with the fleece of my sheep, if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless because I saw that I had support in the gate, then may my arm fall from my shoulder and be torn from its socket.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a righteous man.
Job cares for the poor, the widow, and the fatherless.
Job says, “If I have denied the poor what they desire, I am guilty.
If I have let the widow’s eyes grow dim with hope, I am guilty.
If I have eaten my food alone, I am guilty.
If I have not shared my food with the orphan, I am guilty.
From my youth, I have cared for the orphan as a father.
From my mother’s womb, I have guided the widow.
If I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing, I am guilty.
If I have seen a needy person without a cloak, I am guilty.
If the poor have not blessed me for warming them with the fleece of my sheep, I am guilty.
If I have raised my hand against the fatherless, I am guilty.
If I did this because I saw I had support in the city gate, I am guilty.
If I am guilty of these things, let my shoulder fall from its place.
Let my arm be broken from its socket.”
passages.original: אִם־ אֶ֭מְנַע מֵחֵ֣פֶץ דַּלִּ֑ים וְעֵינֵ֖י אַלְמָנָ֣ה אֲכַלֶּֽה׃ וְאֹכַ֣ל פִּתִּ֣י לְבַדִּ֑י וְלֹא־ אָכַ֖ל יָת֣וֹם מִמֶּֽנָּה׃ כִּ֣י מִ֭נְּעוּרַי גְּדֵלַ֣נִי כְאָ֑ב וּמִבֶּ֖טֶן אִמִּ֣י אַנְחֶֽנָּה׃ אִם־ אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֭וֹבֵד מִבְּלִ֣י לְב֑וּשׁ וְאֵ֥ין כְּ֝ס֗וּת לָאֶבְיֽוֹן׃ אִם־ לֹ֣א בֵרֲכ֣וּנִי חֲלָצוֹ וּמִגֵּ֥ז כְּ֝בָשַׂי יִתְחַמָּֽם׃ אִם־ הֲנִיפ֣וֹתִי עַל־ יָת֣וֹם יָדִ֑י כִּֽי־ אֶרְאֶ֥ה בַ֝שַּׁ֗עַר עֶזְרָתִֽי׃ כְּ֭תֵפִי מִשִּׁכְמָ֣ה תִפּ֑וֹל וְ֝אֶזְרֹעִ֗י מִקָּנָ֥ה תִשָּׁבֵֽר׃

passages.text: For calamity from God terrifies me, and His splendor I cannot overpower.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful.
God can bring calamity.
Calamity from God terrifies me.
God’s splendor is great.
I cannot overpower His splendor.
passages.original: כִּ֤י פַ֣חַד אֵ֭לַי אֵ֣יד אֵ֑ל וּ֝מִשְּׂאֵת֗וֹ לֹ֣א אוּכָֽל׃

passages.text: If I have put my trust in gold or called pure gold my security, if I have rejoiced in my great wealth because my hand had gained so much, if I have beheld the sun in its radiance or the moon moving in splendor, so that my heart was secretly enticed and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth, this would also be an iniquity to be judged, for I would have denied God on high.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a righteous man who fears God.
Job says, “If I have put my trust in gold, I have sinned.
If I have called pure gold my security, I have sinned.
If I have rejoiced because I had great wealth, I have sinned.
If I have been glad because my hand gained much, I have sinned.
If I have looked at the sun shining brightly, I have sinned.
If I have watched the moon moving in splendor, I have sinned.
If my heart was secretly enticed by these things, I have sinned.
If my hand threw a kiss from my mouth to them, I have sinned.
Doing these things would be a sin to be judged.
If I did these things, I would have denied God who is above.”
passages.original: אִם־ שַׂ֣מְתִּי זָהָ֣ב כִּסְלִ֑י וְ֝לַכֶּ֗תֶם אָמַ֥רְתִּי מִבְטַחִֽי׃ אִם־ אֶ֭שְׂמַח כִּי־ רַ֣ב חֵילִ֑י וְכִֽי־ כַ֝בִּ֗יר מָצְאָ֥ה יָדִֽי׃ אִם־ אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֖וֹר כִּ֣י יָהֵ֑ל וְ֝יָרֵ֗חַ יָקָ֥ר הֹלֵֽךְ׃ וַיִּ֣פְתְּ בַּסֵּ֣תֶר לִבִּ֑י וַתִּשַּׁ֖ק יָדִ֣י לְפִֽי׃ גַּם־ ה֭וּא עָוֺ֣ן פְּלִילִ֑י כִּֽי־ כִחַ֖שְׁתִּי לָאֵ֣ל מִמָּֽעַל׃

passages.text: If I have rejoiced in my enemy’s ruin, or exulted when evil befell him— I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse— if the men of my house have not said, ‘Who is there who has not had his fill?’— but no stranger had to lodge on the street, for my door has been open to the traveler— if I have covered my transgressions like Adam by hiding my guilt in my heart, because I greatly feared the crowds and the contempt of the clans terrified me, so that I kept silent and would not go outside— (Oh, that I had one to hear me! Here is my signature. Let the Almighty answer me; let my accuser compose an indictment.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
Job claims he is righteous in his own eyes.
Job says, “If I rejoiced when my enemy was destroyed, that would be wrong.
If I was glad when trouble came to those who hated me, that would be wrong.
I did not let my mouth sin by cursing my enemy or asking for his death.
If the men of my house did not say, ‘Who has not been satisfied with his food?’ then I would be guilty.
No stranger had to sleep outside my house.
I always opened my door to the traveler.
If I covered my sins as Adam did, that would be wrong.
If I hid my guilt in my heart, that would be wrong.
If I kept silent because I feared the great crowd, that would be wrong.
If I was terrified by the contempt of the clans, that would be wrong.
If I stayed inside and did not go out because of fear, that would be wrong.
Oh, that someone would listen to me!
Here is my signature.
Let the Almighty answer me.
Let my accuser write his charge against me.”
passages.original: אִם־ אֶ֭שְׂמַח בְּפִ֣יד מְשַׂנְאִ֑י וְ֝הִתְעֹרַ֗רְתִּי כִּֽי־ מְצָ֥אוֹ רָֽע׃ וְלֹא־ נָתַ֣תִּי לַחֲטֹ֣א חִכִּ֑י לִשְׁאֹ֖ל בְּאָלָ֣ה נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃ אִם־ לֹ֣א אָ֭מְרוּ מְתֵ֣י אָהֳלִ֑י מִֽי־ יִתֵּ֥ן מִ֝בְּשָׂר֗וֹ לֹ֣א נִשְׂבָּֽע׃ בַּ֭חוּץ לֹא־ יָלִ֣ין גֵּ֑ר דְּ֝לָתַ֗י לָאֹ֥רַח אֶפְתָּֽח׃ אִם־ כִּסִּ֣יתִי כְאָדָ֣ם פְּשָׁעָ֑י לִטְמ֖וֹן בְּחֻבִּ֣י עֲוֺֽנִי׃ כִּ֤י אֶֽעֱר֨וֹץ׀ הָ֘מ֤וֹן רַבָּ֗ה וּבוּז־ מִשְׁפָּח֥וֹת יְחִתֵּ֑נִי וָ֝אֶדֹּ֗ם לֹא־ אֵ֥צֵא פָֽתַח׃ מִ֤י יִתֶּן־ לִ֨י׀ שֹׁ֘מֵ֤עַֽ לִ֗י הֶן־ תָּ֭וִי שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲנֵ֑נִי וְסֵ֥פֶר כָּ֝תַ֗ב אִ֣ישׁ רִיבִֽי׃

passages.text: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder and wear it like a crown.
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
Job is a righteous man.
Job says he would carry the indictment on his shoulder.
He would wear it like a crown.
passages.original: אִם־ לֹ֣א עַל־ שִׁ֭כְמִי אֶשָּׂאֶ֑נּוּ אֶֽעֶנְדֶ֖נּוּ עֲטָר֣וֹת לִֽי׃

passages.text: I would give account of all my steps; I would approach Him like a prince.)— if my land cries out against me and its furrows weep together, if I have devoured its produce without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants, then let briers grow instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley.” Thus conclude the words of Job.
passages.sermon:
Job is the speaker.
Job is a righteous man who suffers greatly.
Job says, “I would give account of all my steps.
I would approach God like a prince.
If my land cries out against me,
If its furrows weep together,
If I have eaten its produce without paying,
If I have broken the spirit of its tenants,
Then let briers grow instead of wheat.
Let stinkweed grow instead of barley.
These are the last words of Job.”
passages.original: מִסְפַּ֣ר צְ֭עָדַי אַגִּידֶ֑נּוּ כְּמוֹ־ נָ֝גִ֗יד אֲקָרֲבֶֽנּוּ׃ אִם־ עָ֭לַי אַדְמָתִ֣י תִזְעָ֑ק וְ֝יַ֗חַד תְּלָמֶ֥יהָ יִבְכָּיֽוּן׃ אִם־ כֹּ֭חָהּ אָכַ֣לְתִּי בְלִי־ כָ֑סֶף וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ בְּעָלֶ֣יהָ הִפָּֽחְתִּי׃ תַּ֤חַת חִטָּ֨ה׀ יֵ֥צֵא ח֗וֹחַ וְתַֽחַת־ שְׂעֹרָ֥ה בָאְשָׁ֑ה תַּ֝֗מּוּ דִּבְרֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃פ
